the relaxation of a quantum dot molecule is dominated by phonons and occurs on a ps time scale.

the influence of the electronphonon coupling on the dynamics of a quantum dot molecule.

the phonons play an essential role for the dynamics in quantum dot molecules, and that the relaxation of the electron population between the dots is a non-Markovian process, which is strongly dependent on the energy mismatch.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quantum dot molecule is an excellent candidate for studying quantum decoherence in a solid state system.
the electron-phonon interaction is responsible for the fast decay of the electron coherence in quantum dots and that the decoherence rate is strongly enhanced in the case of a quantum dot molecule.
we have shown how phonon assisted tunneling can be used to control the relaxation dynamics and the decoherence of the system, and thus the efficiency of quantum information processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron-phonon interaction can be treated in a fully non-perturbational manner in order to describe the dynamics in the presence of a strong electron-phonon coupling.
the phonon-induced decoherence in the quantum dot molecule is a very fast process and that the electron-phonon interaction is the main source of decoherence in the system.
the electron-phonon coupling is a crucial ingredient in order to describe the relaxation and decoherence of the electron dynamics in doped quantum dot molecules.
